How DORAi works, in four scenes

01

    One resource, one change, one register entry

    These are the real DORAi screens, recorded on its FinPay sample. Follow the payments database from a cloud scan to a draft export.

      How to use DORAi

      DORAi keeps the register that DORA asks financial firms for: which technology providers you depend on, and for what. These are the steps, in the order you do them.

      1. Set up once

        You
        Enter your firm, providers, contracts with their services, and business functions under Register items. Tag cloud resources with dora-contract and dora-function.
        DORAi
        Stores who typed each value and builds the 15 register templates from those items.
        You end up with
        A register with your facts in it, and empty cells where facts are still missing.

      2. Scan your cloud

        You
        Open Cloud inventory and press Scan clouds. A row opens to show its tags and contract.
        DORAi
        Reads resources from Azure and AWS without changing them, and links them to the services you entered.
        You end up with
        An inventory, plus countries and estimated costs for linked services. A scan never creates a contract or provider.

      3. Check a change

        You
        Save a Terraform plan as JSON, choose it under Change findings and press Check plan. In a pipeline, run dorai check.
        DORAi
        Runs five fixed rules. The pipeline fails on a High finding. AI can word an explanation in the app, but cannot change a finding.
        You end up with
        A list of problems before anything is deployed, each naming the template it affects. The register stays as it was.

      4. Review suggestions

        You
        Open AI review, press Get AI suggestions, read the reason and the source, then press Accept or Reject.
        DORAi
        Drafts four judgement cells, and suggests a service type or function for resources without one.
        You end up with
        Accepted judgement cells in the register, under your name. An accepted type or function is only recorded, so enter it on the service yourself.

      5. Fill the gaps and export

        You
        Click Add in an empty register cell. Open Validation & export, clear every error, then save the package and the report.
        DORAi
        Names each failing cell. While required cells are missing, the package’s file name starts with DRAFT.
        You end up with
        An xBRL-CSV package of 15 templates and a PDF. In 1.1.1 some basic errors, such as a bad LEI, don’t force a draft, so check the error count is zero.

      The walkthrough above was recorded from DORAi 1.1.1 on its built-in FinPay sample, signed in as a demo reviewer. The AI in the recording is the app’s offline stand-in, so its wording, confidence and citations show the flow, not the quality of a real model. See who fills every column

      Rules decide. AI explains. People confirm.

      Findings come from plain, testable rules. The model classifies, explains and cites. Nothing reaches the register until someone on your team accepts it, and every field shows where it came from.

      Questions, answered straight

      Including the parts DORAi can’t do for you.

      What it does and what you enter →
      Does DORAi fill in the whole register?

      No. Of the 105 columns in our model of the 15 templates, 6 come from the cloud scan and 41 are copied, calculated or defaulted by rules. DORAi can suggest 8 more for a person to accept. The other 50 are yours to enter. See who fills what

      What do we need before the first scan?

      Enter your entity, providers, contracts, services and business functions. Then tag cloud resources with dora-function and dora-contract. A scan adds facts to that register. It does not create contracts or providers. See what you enter

      Can the AI put a wrong value in the regulator’s report?

      Not by itself. A suggestion stays out of the package until a reviewer accepts it. A reviewer can still accept a wrong one, so read the reason and the cited passage first. The PDF may carry an AI-written summary, marked as awaiting confirmation.

      What if the AI has no source?

      It answers “insufficient evidence” and the model is not called. When it does answer, DORAi checks that each cited ID was among the passages it supplied. That proves the source exists. Whether it supports the value is for the reviewer to judge.

      Where do findings come from?

      Five fixed rules: new provider, data location, critical function, untagged resource and new service type. The server and the CLI run the same code. AI can explain a finding, but cannot create one or change its severity.

      What happens when our cloud changes?

      Before deployment, the CLI checks the Terraform plan and fails on High findings. After deployment, a manual or scheduled scan refreshes the values that come from the cloud. The CLI reads a copy of your register, so keep that copy current.

      Which systems can it read?

      Azure, AWS and Terraform plans, plus SaaS apps from Microsoft Entra ID and Okta. Cloud access is read-only. AWS resources that were never tagged need a Resource Explorer index to be found.

      How accurate are costs and locations?

      Both need a check. Cost is an estimate from recent bills, and on AWS it can come out at less than half of the real yearly figure. Processing country means where your resources run, not where the provider’s support staff sit. Read the tradeoffs

      Will the regulator accept the export?

      We can’t promise that. DORAi writes an xBRL-CSV package for EBA DORA taxonomy 4.0, and the team’s Arelle run on the demo package on 21 November 2026 reported no errors. That tests structure and rules, not whether your data is true or complete. Submission stays with your firm.

      Does “ready” mean the register is complete?

      No. It means the rows you entered pass the readiness checks. DORAi cannot know about a contract nobody entered, and in version 1.1.1 even an empty register can pass. See what to check by hand

      Where does our data go?

      Your firm hosts the server and database. With a real AI model turned on, names, tags and the facts behind each question go to the provider you configure. A GLEIF lookup sends the provider’s name or LEI when a reviewer asks for one.

      Do you support groups?

      Partly. The register can hold other entities, branches and intra-group contracts, but a person enters those rows. The forms and automatic defaults are built for a single entity first.

      Run DORAi on your own estate

      Apps for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android connect to a DORAi server your firm hosts. The dorai command line checks plans in CI without a server.
